Alex P: Quick heads-up — I'm working on a small docs PR that clarifies how we signal parsing/validation failures when function/tool calling returns extra fields or array-of-union shapes. Need agreement on the example patterns we ship.
Samir K: +1. Do you mean examples for the JSON-schema guardrails and the parser fallback examples?
Alex P: Yup. Two things: 1) show the canonical normalized shape we expect for arrays of union (wrap-singleton arrays, explicit tag field), 2) a short `on_parse_error` example for SDKs to fall back to raw_text + best-effort parse.
Nina Zhao: For arrays-of-union, can we recommend the explicit discriminator field approach? e.g., { "type": "email", "value": {...} } vs ambiguous union items. It's easier for deterministic parsing. :+1:
Maria (Docs): Agree on discriminator. Also want a tiny snippet showing how to fail gracefully in the hosted API docs — users keep hitting rogue extra keys from LLMs. If you paste a snippet I can slot into the migration guide and link it.
Alex P: Draft snippet — feel free to edit:
```
# canonicalize union-array (py pseudo)
def normalize_items(items):
    out = []
    for it in items:
        if isinstance(it, dict) and 'tag' in it:
            out.append(it)
        elif isinstance(it, dict) and 'type' in it:
            out.append({'tag': it['type'], 'payload': it})
        else:
            # wrap primitives
            out.append({'tag': 'literal', 'payload': it})
    return out
```
Samir K: Nice. For SDK-level fallback we should show both TS and Py tiny examples. For TS: `onParseError: (raw) => ({ fallback: raw.trim() })` — short and practical.
Nina Zhao: One more edge: arrays that sometimes come as single object. Show `if (!Array.isArray(x)) x = [x]` normalization. That avoids lots of customer headaches.
Maria (Docs): I'll add two callouts: "Prefer discriminator fields" and "Normalize singleton->array at ingestion". Also will add a short link to the schema linting action. Can you add the internal link? 
Alex P: Linking to our linting action: https://redwood.inference/internal/actions/schema-lint — add that under "Related tooling".
CI Bot: deploy/preview updated for branch alex/docs-toolcall-parse — preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood.inference/docs/parse-examples (success) :rocket:
Samir K: Quick editorial ask — keep the examples < 12 lines so they fit the quickstart card. Maria, if you want I'll trim the py/ts examples down.
Maria (Docs): Please trim. Also add a one-liner under "Behavioral note": "When in doubt, prefer explicit tags; deterministic parsers are easier to reason about than heuristics."
Alex P: Will prune the snippets and open PR tonight. Thanks all — tagging @Nina Zhao to review the discriminator wording.
Nina Zhao: Happy to review. Small nit — use `kind` instead of `tag`? `kind` maps to other libs we integrate.
Alex P: Good call. I'll switch `tag` -> `kind` across examples.
Maria (Docs): Great. Once PR is up ping me and I'll grab the preview link.
Alex P: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421 — includes trimmed py/ts snippets + link to schema-lint action.
Maria (Docs): Preview looks good, I pushed a tiny wording tweak. Ready to merge after a quick review from @Nina Zhao and @Samir K.
Samir K: Reviewed, lgtm.
Nina Zhao: Reviewed, one comment about the example JSON payload; resolved locally. lgtm.
CI Bot: PR #3421 merged into main by Maria (Docs) — changelog updated.
Alex P: Awesome, thanks team. I'll add a short note to the migration checklist about this pattern.
Maria (Docs): Adding it now: https://redwood.inference/docs/migration/structured-output#array-union-normalization
Alex P: Closing the thread — feel free to reopen if anything pops in staging. :wave:
